run: the user's request of 2026-10-24 (error propagation of the Fourier transform: each r point's error bar of G(r) from F(Q)'s σ, a ribbon on the G(r) panel), built and checked on the committed Demo run, the two local GaTa4Se8 250 K / GaNb4Se8 5 K runs (data/, gitignored), synthetic run folders and the dev cases: arms A, A+ and D on the dev set before (the baseline, validation/baseline/arm-a-dev.json) and after (the code of 117236e, protocol 2026-10-24.4), the model-visible snapshots and the context budget, 2026-10-24
evidence: The user asked (2026-10-24) for the error propagation of the Fourier transform: each r point's error bar of G(r) from F(Q)'s σ, drawn as a ribbon on the G(r) panel when the G(r) data come without error bars. Until now no part of the app could say how large the statistical error of a G(r) point is, so compare_fit's largest residual features were sized only against the data's rms, and whether a residual is above noise could not be answered (the rmc-fit-assessment skill's 'an Rw below the data's noise' had no number to compare with). RMCProfile's transform, established on its own files rather than assumed: the X_ray_exp_renorm column of <stem>_FT_XFQ<n>.csv is sum_k dQ Q_k (F_k + c) sin(Q_k r) over the Q grid of <stem>_XFQ<n>.csv (F_k its F(Q)_Expt column): a rectangle rule with no 2/pi and no rho0 (Keen's D(r) times pi/2), no Lorch, no omitted-low-Q term, c the run's fitted offset recovered by least squares. On the committed Demo run it reproduces the G(r) column to 1.5e-14 of max |G| (c = 2.7258e-4), from the 7-decimal _FQ1.csv to 4.5e-8; every other convention fails by orders of magnitude (the offset left out 3.2e-4, the trapezoid rule of stog/pystog/MATERIA 2.8e-4, with 2/pi 0.36, Lorch 0.21, Keen's G(r) 0.83). The run's F(Q)_Expt is not the input file the .dat names (scale_ft_rmc.fq): it is s K F_input - c, s the fitted scale (FITTED_SCALE), K, with CONVOLVE, the box convolution at R = the last r of <stem>_PDFpartials.csv (the g(r) range: 51.82 A, RMCProfile's 'up to 51.820 A'), (K F)(Q) = 1/(pi Q) sum_j dQ Q_j F_j [sin((Q - Q_j)R)/(Q - Q_j) - sin((Q + Q_j)R)/(Q + Q_j)], a step MATERIA's operator lacks, derived here as the sine transform of F truncated at R and back. On the two local runs (RMCProfile 6.7.9.5) the input reproduces F(Q)_Expt to 4.6e-15 (s = 1.14753505; the log prints 'Renorm 1.1476 Constant = 0.0002') and 6.3e-15 (s = 1.28313083), and the two offsets cancel to 1e-16; without K the best affine fit misses by 0.096, with R = 51.828 (the cell edge) by 3.2e-4. Both reproduction tests pass at RMC_FT_TOLERANCE = 1e-6 of the largest |value|. σ comes only from the input file's own third column, clean by usable_sigma's rule, times s; the Demo's input file is not committed and neither local input file has a σ column, so on every real run on hand the panel says why there is no ribbon ('F(Q) carries no uncertainties: scale_ft_rmc.fq (named in GTS_250K.dat) is not in the run folder' on the Demo). The propagation is exact for the linear transform: Cov[G(r), G(r')] = sum_k (dQ Q_k s σ_k)^2 sin(Q_k r) sin(Q_k r') = 1/2 [P(r - r') - P(r + r')], the ribbon its diagonal, the caption saying the points are correlated (rho = 0.97 between neighbours, about 62 independent points of 1767 on the Demo's grids for a σ rising with Q). The box convolution is left out of the propagation: at r well inside R it removes only noise beyond R (it lowers σ by at most 0.19 % at r <= 20 A on the Demo's grids), checked exactly at nine points nearest r_max with a 1 % limit. Known answers: a brute-force Jacobian, Monte Carlo (20 000 draws, also through K), white noise against the continuum integral, the Nyquist grid's exact orthogonality, the continuum correlation law, MATERIA's pystog golden adapted to RMCProfile's convention (G_RMC = (pi/2) G_pystog + the rectangle's endpoint halves, sigma_RMC^2 = (pi/2)^2 dG^2 + dQ^2 (e_0 + e_n)/2, both to 1e-12), RMCProfile's StoG on FeCoSn 199 K (data-gated). Python and the browser give one payload (ft_uncertainty_fixture.json, 1e-9). Arms A, A+ and D on the dev set before and after: all 45 records identical in verdict, score, readings and truth (they do not call compare_fit), so the baseline is not re-recorded. What the model sees changes in compare_fit only: its description (+56 tokens on the dock's and arm B's worst turns; 48k headroom 5,200 and 7,999 tokens) and, for an X-ray G(r), its result (the Demo's: 'No σ(r) for this G(r) (F(Q) carries no uncertainties: ...): whether a residual feature is above noise is not judged.'; dev-fit-unconverged's has no .dat). The test set was not run. Approved by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-24.
proposed_fix: rmc_toolkits/ft_uncertainty.py (the source of truth, exported): rmc_ft, rmc_ft_sigma, rmc_ft_covariance, correlation_summary, box_convolution, convolution_sigma_change, reproduce_transform, reproduce_input, run_datasets, file_sigma_column, assess_ft_uncertainty (arrays to the payload {status propagated | unavailable | failed, reason, sigma, transform, reproduction, convolutionCheck, correlation, sources}) and ft_uncertainty_for_run (the run folder: <stem>.dat, the input file it names, <stem>_XFQ<n>.csv else _FQ<n>.csv, <stem>_PDFpartials.csv); RMC_FT_TOLERANCE 1e-6, CONVOLUTION_CHECK_LIMIT 0.01. Flask's /api/plot/data adds it to an xPDF plot as `uncertainty` (_ft_uncertainty: a _FileCache keyed on the transform and its companions' signatures, the input file read only inside the data roots, a read failure a failed payload, never a 500), and a column whose header names an uncertainty becomes the experimental series' sigma (_xpdf_sigma, clean by usable_sigma's rule). The browser: src/ftUncertainty.js (the port) and src/ftUncertaintyRun.js (the run glue over every picked file, makeRunFromEntries' allFiles; one payload per set of file versions), attached to each parsed xPDF plot (the Dashboard's parse rounds, openRunFolder); parity golden ft_uncertainty_fixture.json (tests/generate_ft_uncertainty_fixture.py: the Demo and twelve synthetic run folders, every outcome), plot parity pinned on an xPDF file with a σ column. The Dashboard: InteractivePlot's opt-in ribbon prop (a band under the experiment, inside the y range, in the legend, ± σ in the readout); grRibbon.js / GrRibbon.jsx: the propagated ribbon when the G(r) file has no σ, else the file's with the propagated one as a header toggle, a caption that says the r points are correlated, its ? help and title giving the transform, both reproduction residuals with the tolerance, the correlation and the convolution check; no σ, the caption says why; a failure also a Problems-section warning; Live Data re-reads it with its files (Flask: plotDataVersion over the transform, the .dat, the F(Q) and PDFpartials files). compare_fit (src/llm/copilot/runTools.js): for an X-ray G(r), σ(r) from the file's own σ else the propagated one; each largest residual feature's relative_to_sigma and above_noise (>= ABOVE_NOISE_SIGMA = 3 σ), data.noise (sigma, from, rms_residual_over_sigma, above_noise_at, reproduction {residual, tolerance}, correlation {neighbour, effective_points, points}) and a note ('Against σ(r) propagated from ...: k of the n largest residual features are above noise ...; the residual's rms is ... σ. The r points are correlated ...: adjacent points beyond σ are one feature, not several.'); a G(r) whose σ is known to be unavailable gets noise {sigma: null, why} and 'No σ(r) for this G(r) (...): whether a residual feature is above noise is not judged.'. The model-visible snapshots (dock/tools.json, the new tool-results/compare_fit.xpdf.json, dev-fit-unconverged's record) and the context-budget pins are updated. PROTOCOL_VERSION 2026-10-24.4. Docs: docs/algorithms/run-dashboard.md ('The G(r) error ribbon'), docs/ALGORITHMS.md, ai-assistant.md (compare_fit's σ(r) reading), REFERENCE.md, AGENTS.md. Left open: committing the Demo run's input file (data/250K_try1/scale_ft_rmc.fq) as a test fixture would run the input-to-F(Q) chain test in CI (data-gated today, as the repo's other real-data tests); a run whose input file carries σ is needed to see a propagated ribbon on real data.
